workflow.primaryIntent: Review what PowerMyMac calls junk before removing Mac storage categories; distinguish cache, attachments and backups.
workflow.title: Review PowerMyMac's junk categories before cleaning your Mac
workflow.description: A review checklist for PowerMyMac's Junk Cleaner categories: separate caches from attachments and backups, then decide what you can afford to remove or rebuild.
outline: Answer first: a scan category is not deletion permission; show official result-review image immediately after lead once rights clear.
Explain documented scan -> category review -> file selection -> CLEAN without claiming to have run it.
Separate recoverable caches from email attachments and device backups; do not recommend Select All.
Ask who owns the data, whether a backup exists, and what re-download/rebuild cost means; mark these as editorial checklist questions.
Document what is unknown about deletion/recovery; do not turn the Shredder feature into a cache-cleaning recommendation.
Choose category-based cleanup versus investigating why storage returns; one bounded recommendation with Breathing Room affiliation and preview/hosted/Python caveats.
Show current-source Space example preview later with its full disclosure and link to concise comparison.
workflow.distinctness: Category-level decision workflow, not an expanded feature matrix or a second PowerMyMac alias page. No invented duplicate-file test or savings benchmark.
workflow.interactionHandoff: Read-only keep/review checklist keyed to cache, original attachment and backup, with no default delete choices and no scan/upload/cleanup execution.
workflow.targetLength: 900-1400 words if earned; do not pad
